proposal_subtitle: An AI and digital transformation proposal: strategy first, then build.

paragraphs: Meridian Health Group delivers aged care and community care services across New South Wales. Your care, rostering, finance and HR teams each rely on a different system, and none of them talks to the others. The same information is typed in several times, and compliance reporting is assembled by hand.

Your leadership team is hearing a lot about AI, and several vendors have already pitched. What's missing is an independent view of where AI genuinely pays back, how it fits your regulatory obligations, and who owns the change. You asked us for that view before committing capital.

client_quote.text: We keep buying software and the manual work just moves somewhere else.
client_quote.attribution: Chief Operating Officer, Meridian Health Group (from our discovery call)

challenges.title: Systems that don't connect
challenges.description: Four core systems, no shared data. Admissions, rosters and funding claims are re-keyed by hand.

challenges.title: Reporting by hand
challenges.description: SIRS and Care Minutes data is assembled from several sources every cycle, adding effort and compliance risk.

challenges.title: AI without direction
challenges.description: Vendor pitches and internal enthusiasm, but no agreed use cases, owner or governance.

challenges.title: Change fatigue
challenges.description: Staff have lived through tools that added work. Adoption has to be designed in, not hoped for.

readiness_snapshot.note: Core care processes are documented at some sites, but each site runs them differently.
The care, rostering, finance and HR systems share no data layer; information moves by re-keying and spreadsheets.
A few scheduled exports exist. Intake, rostering and reporting steps are almost entirely manual.

vision.headline: From four disconnected systems to one joined-up operation
from_points: Information is typed in again at every handover
Compliance reports are built by hand each cycle
AI is pitched tool by tool, without a plan
New software lands without a change plan
to_points: Enter it once; it flows to rostering, finance and reporting
Reports assembled from live records and reviewed by your people
A ranked, costed AI roadmap with clear guardrails
Roles remapped and teams trained before go-live

options_intro: You don't have to commit to the whole journey. Each option stands on its own, and each earns the right to the next. We recommend starting with Path A, because the biggest risk in any AI programme is building the wrong thing.

options.name: Discovery & Assessment
options.tagline: A fast, evidence-based read of where AI and process change will actually pay back.
options.who_for: Best for validating scope before committing further budget.
includes: 7-pillar AI maturity scorecard and executive risk summary
Application and workflow audit across your four core systems
Target operating architecture and buy-vs-build recommendation
Costed roadmap and ROI business case for the build phase

options.name: Foundation Proof-of-Value
options.tagline: Prove the highest-value workflow works end to end, before you scale it.
options.who_for: Best for a working proof on your highest-value care workflow.
includes: Production-grade build of one priority workflow, such as rostering to payroll
Integration with your existing care management and finance systems
Telemetry, security sign-off and a production blueprint
Staff walkthroughs and a Day-30 results review

options.name: Enterprise Transformation
options.tagline: Roll the proven approach across your care operations, with change management built in.
options.who_for: Best for a full rollout across sites, with adoption and hypercare.
includes: Multi-workflow build and integration across the operating stack
ADKAR change management, role remapping and training sandboxes

options_note: Paths B and C are planning estimates built from hours and rates. We reconfirm them at the end of Stage 2, once the architecture is signed off.

add_ons.title: Fractional CIO / CTO / PMO

add_ons.price_label: Scoped with the option you choose

add_ons.title: AI governance & ISO 42001 design
add_ons.description: An AI management-system operating model, policy pack and risk taxonomy aligned to ISO 42001 and APRA CPS 234 / APP.

add_ons.title: Buy vs build feasibility sprint
add_ons.description: An evaluation matrix, API capability assessment and three-year TCO model before you commit to a platform or a build.

plan.headline: Path A: three weeks to a costed roadmap
plan.intro: We recommend starting with Discovery & Assessment. It covers the first two stages of our operating system, gives you a signed-off baseline and blueprint, and may be fully offset by AWS funding, subject to approval. Later stages are shown so you can see where it leads.

1: Stakeholder interviews across care, finance, HR and IT
Ground-truth audit of the systems and workflows your staff actually use
7-pillar AI maturity scorecard and executive risk summary
2: Target process architecture and swimlane maps
Buy-vs-build view and ranked AI use-case shortlist
Costed roadmap and ROI business case for Path B or C
3: Build and integrate the prioritised workflows
Legacy data migration and API middleware
User acceptance testing and zero-downtime cutover
4: ADKAR role remapping and training sandboxes
Day-30 review and ongoing assurance retainer

investment_note: All figures exclude GST. Path A is a fixed fee. Paths B and C are planning estimates, reconfirmed at the end of Stage 2. Ongoing AWS infrastructure and API usage costs are separate from these professional-services fees.
assumptions: Meridian provides timely access to relevant systems, documentation and subject-matter experts throughout the engagement.
Scope covers the care, rostering, finance and HR systems named in this proposal. Other systems are out of scope unless agreed in writing.
AWS funding is subject to AWS's own review and eligibility. DD Consulting submits the application but does not control AWS's decision or timeline.
Path B and Path C figures are planning estimates and are reconfirmed before any work begins.
Cloud hosting, API usage and software licences remain Meridian's direct responsibility.

friction_matrix.friction: Assessment data is re-typed into the rostering and finance systems.
Shift changes are phoned through and updated by hand; skills and credentials are checked manually.
friction_matrix.impact: Coordinator time lost to manual dispatch.

friction_matrix.friction: Progress notes are captured on paper at some sites and keyed in later.
SIRS and Care Minutes data is assembled by hand from several systems.
friction_matrix.impact: Days of preparation each reporting cycle.

friction_matrix.friction: Funding claims are reconciled manually against care records.

target_state.requirement: One source of truth for care and roster data
target_state.solution: An integration layer that syncs admissions, rosters and finance, so information is entered once.
Automated assembly of SIRS and Care Minutes data from live records, with human review before submission.

target_state.requirement: AI where it pays back, under clear guardrails
target_state.solution: Prioritised use cases with deterministic policy checks and human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk decisions, aligned to ISO 42001.
Staged releases, audit logging and Australian data residency in AWS Sydney (ap-southeast-2).

aws_footprint.function: Connects care, rostering, finance and HR systems through one event-driven layer.
Runs workflows such as roster changes and reporting assembly, with deterministic rules.
Reads and drafts from unstructured content under human review. No decisions are delegated to the model.
Governed data store for the integrated care and roster record.
Role-based access, encryption and a full audit trail.

aws_funding_details.driver: Fragmented care systems, manual compliance reporting and readiness for AI adoption
